headline: PM Tarique Rahman: Killers of anti-fascist movement to be tried transparently
summary: The Prime Minister inaugurated the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum and vowed that those responsible for killings during the uprising would face impartial trials.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has announced that those responsible for killings during the July Mass Uprising will be brought to justice through transparent, impartial, and credible trials.
The Prime Minister made these remarks while inaugurating the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum at Gono Bhaban in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.
He emphasized that justice for every crime is essential to ensure the rule of law and that trials will be conducted in accordance with the due process of law.

The government has also decided to name institutions in local areas after every person who was killed or subjected to enforced disappearance over the past 17 years, including victims of the July movement.
Tarique Rahman stated that the newly opened museum should not be used to promote the political narratives of any individual, group, or party.
He asserted that the 2024 mass uprising belonged to the democratic people of Bangladesh, rather than any specific political entity.
Comparing the two historic events, the PM noted that while the 1971 Liberation War secured independence, the 2024 uprising was fought to protect that independence and the people's freedom.

headline: Former NCP leader sent to jail over Facebook posts on PM
summary: Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir was pelted with eggs by Chhatra Dal activists in Bogura after a court ordered him to be sent to jail.
details: Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir, a former leader of the National Citizens Party (NCP), was sent to jail by a Bogura court on Wednesday. As he was being transported to prison in a police pickup van, he was pelted with eggs by Chhatra Dal activists.

The incident occurred around 12:30 PM at the Bogura Chief Judicial Magistrate Court premises. The activists, including members from Bogura City Chhatra Dal and various college branches, had gathered to express their anger.

Sandhan Sarkar, president of the Bogura District Chhatra Dal, admitted to the act, stating that the activists were outraged by Tanvir's defamatory and offensive Facebook posts about the Prime Minister.
Tanvir was arrested early Wednesday morning from the Monipur area of Dhaka by Bogura District Police. He had been temporarily removed from the NCP on July 31 following the controversial posts.
A case was filed against him on August 2 under the Cyber Security Act at Bogura Sadar Police Station by Maftun Ahmed Khan, president of the Bogura Sadar Upazila BNP.
Previously, Tanvir had been temporarily removed from the party in April 2025 due to allegations of commission-trading in DC appointments and textbook printing, though that order was later withdrawn.

Tanvir was arrested early Wednesday morning from the Monipur area of Dhaka by Bogura District Police. He had been temporarily removed from the NCP on July 31 following the controversial posts.
